body:
ADR-SHAPED PROPOSAL for bd-01M15TBYEHT8DDWZSYJFPGQCPZ: retain adapter-owned receipt contexts now; do not add a portable sensitivity field to PropositionEvidence yet.

CONTEXT AND DECISION. The privacy defect was real: chart structure can encode transcript-derived material, and a plain structural checksum permits a candidate-material dictionary attack. The landed StructuralReceiptContext closes that defect without pretending ChartOrigin can classify disclosure. The same Hand origin names both public fixtures and researcher-reviewed participant material. I recommend recording the narrow boundary as the current architecture and closing this design bead without implementation. Neither reopening signal is present today: embed-grakern is the only chart provider making a plain-versus-keyed choice, and no consumer outside it has had to reconstruct that choice from insufficient evidence.

WHY NOT PUT SENSITIVITY ON PROPOSITION EVIDENCE NOW. Sensitivity is not a semantic property of a proposition or an acquisition origin. It is a classification of material under a disclosure policy. The same structural chart may be public after authorized release, internal during curation, or sensitive when derived from a participant transcript. Canonical chart identity deliberately excludes provenance and must also exclude confidentiality. More importantly, the repository currently has no portable authority from which PropositionEvidence could derive this field: StorySource, PropositionChart, ChartProvenance, RecallUnit, and PropositionEvidence carry no material-classification chain. Adding a mandatory field would therefore ask each caller to make the same assertion that StructuralReceiptContext asks for now, but farther from the operation that needs it. Making the case class public or adding copy would also create a trivial downgrade path. A typed but ungrounded Public assertion is not stronger evidence.

OPTION A — PORTABLE FIELD, HONEST BENEFITS. A mandatory classification travelling with each PropositionEvidence would eliminate drift between evidence and a separately supplied context, let heterogeneous batches derive their sensitivity mechanically, and give every future chart provider one join law. A provider could not accidentally omit classification at its call site. This becomes attractive when a second chart provider repeats the grakern boundary or an external consumer must decide digest kind.

OPTION A — DEPENDENCY AND MIGRATION COST. The existing Sensitivity enum lives in embed-core. proposition must not depend on embed-core: it would invert the semantic-to-provider layering, and embed-core already reaches proposition through acquire. A portable implementation should move or generalize the vocabulary into core, which both proposition and embed-core already depend on, then preserve the storymodel4s.embed source surface with an alias or export during migration. PropositionEvidence would need a private, mandatory classification with no default; every of and hand constructor becomes source-breaking. It should not be added to ChartProvenance, because origin and disclosure are orthogonal. A trustworthy version also needs classification to originate at StorySource or another explicit material boundary and to propagate monotonically; adding only the leaf field leaves it self-asserted.

OPTION A — CODEC AND RECEIPT COST. There is currently no PropositionEvidence codec, and the RecallUnit codec omits its optional evidence entirely. A field on the Scala type would therefore evaporate on existing wire paths unless the whole evidence container is versioned and added to recall/source codecs. Legacy JSON with no classification must never decode as Public. It must either be rejected with a typed migration error or decoded as an explicit Unclassified top state that receipt-producing adapters refuse until classified. Classification must remain outside Canonical.checksum and semantic equality, but it must enter receipt item identity. Grakern preparation would change from charts to classified evidence, derive source sensitivity as the join of every prepared source, and derive row/output sensitivity as query joined with all prepared sources. Its memoization key would need at least chart checksum plus sensitivity and key authority; otherwise the same chart first seen Public could lend a plain receipt to a later Sensitive use. StructuralReceiptContext would still be needed for the key authority, though no longer for duplicate classification.

OPTION B — ADAPTER-OWNED CONTEXT, HONEST BENEFITS AND COSTS. The landed design is narrow, has no codec migration, does not contaminate semantic identity, and places the disclosure decision exactly where material becomes a provider receipt. Construction requires both source and query classifications, has no implicit Public value, snapshots one key authority, and fails before computation when non-public material lacks a key. Its cost is repetition: another chart provider could invent a slightly different context or join rule; classification is separate from the evidence and could drift; heterogeneous queries require partitioning or a conservative cohort declaration. Those costs are real, but they are prospective today rather than duplicated production code.

REQUIRED LAW FOR EITHER OPTION. Sensitivity forms the ordered join Public less than Internal less than Sensitive. Every input, cache artifact, and output is classified at the maximum of all material that contributes to it. For grakern, a row depends on the query and the entire prepared source dictionary, not merely the ultimately selected node, so output sensitivity joins query with all prepared sources. Mixed cohorts either partition by classification and key authority or declare the whole cohort at the maximum. They never choose the minimum for reproducibility. Classification never affects alignment scores, proposition identity, graph identity, or scientific equality.

FAIL-CLOSED RULES FOR THE CURRENT ADAPTER DESIGN. No context default; no inference from ChartOrigin, fixture location, hand review, or provider name. Missing classification is a construction error. Any non-public side requires a captured key at context construction; missing key means no compute, cache entry, or provider receipt. Plain identity is admissible only when both source and query are explicitly Public. Contexts are immutable; memoization and receipt logs never cross context or key snapshots. If actual inputs are more sensitive than the cohort declaration, callers must rebuild at the maximum rather than reuse a lower context. Receipt items retain their declared classification, digest kind, and key id.

REOPENING AND TARGET SHAPE. Reopen when either a second proposition-chart provider must reproduce this decision or a consumer outside embed-grakern cannot ground plain-versus-keyed from what it holds. At that point, do not merely add a third field to the current public case class. Introduce one core material-classification vocabulary and a non-downgradable classified-evidence construction rooted at the source/material boundary; derive composites by join; require an explicit declassification policy receipt for any downward transition; version the evidence codecs; reject or explicitly mark legacy unclassified material; and migrate grakern to derive classification while retaining adapter-owned key authority.

VISION CHECK. This recommendation keeps exact evidence and scientific semantics independent of operational secrecy while making the receipt decision explicit, auditable, and falsifiable. It avoids manufacturing a portable fact the current model cannot derive, preserves public reproducibility, and still fails closed for participant material. Recommendation: ADR 0001 should record the adapter-owned rule, the join and fail-closed laws above, and the two reopening signals; no code now. Chief and scout: please attack the recommendation, especially whether the lack of a source-rooted classification makes a portable field premature or instead argues for widening this bead to StorySource.
